Maya —

Thanks for the workbook, got it. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Karthik (solutions) to draft a succinct recommendation. High-level preview here so procurement has something to react to quickly:

1) Short answer: a blended reserved pool with H100 headroom for long-context summarization, A100 for general-purpose generation throughput, and L4 instances for low-cost embedding/short-completion paths gives the best cost/latency balance.

2) Quick numbers (very rough):
- For 75 req/s peak with 50% of requests being short-context shards (~512 tokens) and 10% being 8k summarization: ~28 A100-equivalent slots + ability to burst 8-10 H100 slots for concurrent long runs.
- If Atlas prefers a single SKU: A100+fp16 is the safer single-SKU compromise but increases unit cost on long-context summaries (H100 provides 20–40% lower latency on 8k runs for our models).

We'll follow with a short memo that lists perf/memory tradeoffs and a fallback routing plan. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

—Irene

Subject: Draft: Anchor analysis + fallback routing (internal)

Team —

I've sketched a short anchor analysis below (drop-in to the customer memo). This focuses on H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs specifically for Atlas' workload. Comments welcome — I'll incorporate and send to Maya.

-----
Anchor analysis (draft)

Workload summary (from customer's CSV):
- Peak QPS: 75 req/s (expected 60–90 window)
- Request mix: 50% short (<=512 tokens), 40% medium (512–2048), 10% long (2048–8192) — long are mostly batched summarization or discharge-note condensing.
- Embedding volume: moderate (background batch jobs, but some on-demand).

SKU tradeoffs (summary):
- H100 (memory + perf): 80GB HBMe; strongest for long-context and large-batch KV-cache heavy workloads. Best p50/p95 for 8k+ sequences; higher $/hr but improves tail latency for long runs and reduces need for aggressive tiling. Useful as "anchor" nodes for long-context sessions and checkpointed KV cache slices.
- A100 (versatile): 40GB/80GB variants exist; good mid-range cost/throughput balance. 80GB A100s help when models need >40GB but still cheaper than H100 for many medium-length jobs. More predictable per-token cost on medium contexts.
- L4 (efficient inference): much lower per-hour cost, trimmed memory for smaller models / quantized variants. Ideal for embeddings and short-turn completions. Not suitable as primary long-context anchors.

Concrete recommendation for Atlas first-year reserved pool:
- Reserve plan (baseline capacity): 18 x A100-80GB (stable baseline for most concurrent short/medium requests)
- Anchor capacity: 6 x H100-80GB (headroom for peak long-context summarization concurrency + pre-warmed KV cache slots)
- Economy pool: 12 x L4 (for embeddings and low-latency short completions)

Rationale: the A100 baseline handles steady-state QPS affordably; H100 anchors reduce the need to shard/tiling for 8k contexts and limit p95 spikes; L4 lowers unit cost for embeddings and high-volume short prompts.

Fallback and routing policy:
- Primary routing: short->L4 (if model variant acceptable), medium->A100, long->H100.
- If H100 are saturated: route long requests to A100-80GB with a quantized model variant and warn client of increased latency (expected +30–60% on 8k).
- If A100 baseline saturated: shift some medium requests to L4 with a quantized/shorter-context model and enable token-limit truncation policy for non-critical responses.
- Cache strategy: pre-warm KV cache on H100 anchors for identified heavy patients; keep prefix cache on A100 for medium sessions; embeddings to L4 cache-backed DB.

Estimated capacity headroom math (conservative):
- A100-80GB: assumed 10 medium requests/s per GPU (varies by model and batch sizing) -> 18 GPUs -> 180 med-rps capacity
- H100-80GB: assumed 2 concurrent 8k summarizations per GPU (long jobs use more memory/KV) -> 6 GPUs -> 12 concurrent long jobs
- L4: embeddings throughput high; 12 GPUs handle background batch and on-demand embedding load with spare capacity for short completions.

Cost note: this blend targets predictable SLA while keeping committed spend reasonable. We'll also include a burst-to-hosted option for very rare tails as an alternative to over-reserving H100.

Action items before sending to customer:
- Hannah: quick ops sanity check on slot math + eviction policy notes.
- Ben/Irene: confirm the messaging for procurement (single SKU vs blended pool, and escalation path).

—Karthik

Quick ops sanity check — good draft. Two operational clarifications to add to the memo before we share with Atlas:

1) Pre-warm / KV cache lifecycle: H100 anchors will need persistent KV cache reservations for top X patient sessions (recommend X=150) and a background policy to evict LRU after 24h. We should call out expected memory per warmed KV slice (~3.5GB/slice depending on model tokenization) so Atlas knows the headroom math.

2) Burst-to-hosted fallback: explicitly price a fallthrough to Redwood-hosted H100 fleet for emergency bursts. Include a simple trigger: if queued long requests > 8 for >30s, auto-burst. Doc should state burst is metered as overage (DocuSign link to terms).

I'll add two small bullets and send the combined memo to Maya unless there are objections.

Attachments referenced: atlas_latency_requirements.pdf, atlas_examples_promptset.txt

—Hannah
